label:
Still-residue
cheese (shuurmg)
comment: Cheese made from what the still leaves behind.

about.text: What is left in the pot after soured milk has been distilled into milk spirit. Kalmyks call it bozo and press it into a curd, aadmag, which is made into dried cakes, or use it to dress hides; Mongolian herders dry the mash into aaruul.

links.name: Stepnye Vesti (Kalmyk newspaper), 'O molochnoi pishche i napitkakh kalmykov'

how.text: Nothing is added: the heated, soured milk curd stays in the pot while the alcohol leaves. It is pressed by hand or bagged, drained and dried in the sun.

links.name: Cambridge Kalmyk Cultural Heritage: Purvya Volod'kina, Milk Products and Vodka

steps.note: Hung in cloth bags outside while the whey drips out, and the solids dry in the sun.
Dried further into shuurmg, the dried cheese.
